age.evidence: three mice were 20 wk old and one mouse was 28 wk old... Two additional male mice of the same strain (19 wk old)

sex.evidence: Four adult C57BL/6J mice (JAX 000664), two male and two female, were used for electrophysiological recordings... Two additional male mice of the same strain (19 wk old) were used to evaluate head-twitch responses under DOI.

dosing.evidence: injected 2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine, (±)-DOI hydrochloride... subcutaneously at a concentration of 10 mg/kg (diluted in sterile saline)... We performed electrophysiological recordings on five different days for each mouse.

assays.assay_description: Rate of head-twitches counted in freely moving mice in their home cage 20 min after DOI (10 mg/kg s.c.) or saline injection, used to confirm dose effectiveness.

application_type.evidence: subcutaneously at a concentration of 10 mg/kg

food_restriction.evidence: freely moving in their cage (home cage)

water_restriction.evidence: freely moving in their cage (home cage)

time_to_assay.evidence: Twenty minutes after injection of DOI, these mice showed a rate of 2 HTR/min

sample_size.evidence: Two additional male mice of the same strain (19 wk old) were used to evaluate head-twitch responses under DOI.

outcomes.summary: DOI (10 mg/kg s.c.) increased head-twitch response rate to ~2 HTR/min and 1.8 HTR/min in the two mice, compared with 0.2 HTR/min after saline injection, confirming dose effectiveness.
outcomes.evidence: Twenty minutes after injection of DOI, these mice showed a rate of 2 HTR/min and 1.8 HTR/min, compared to 0.2 HTR/min for either mouse after saline injection.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single rate (HTR/min) reported; no within-session time course

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is treated as HTR/WDS, not ethological per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: No pose-estimation or ML classifier described for HTR scoring

E6_spatial.evidence: home cage as single open space

E7_social_context.evidence: Paper does not indicate co-housing during HTR scoring; treated as individual home-cage observation

E8_food_water.evidence: Home cage testing; food and water typically accessible in home cage

D1_continuity.evidence: Single HTR observation period after injection

D2_session_duration.evidence: HTR/min rate reported but duration not explicitly stated; treated as brief observation

D3_recording_days.evidence: HTR measurement on single day not stated otherwise

D6_circadian.evidence: Brief observation, far less than 6 h

judge_notes: Dropped all electrophysiology/auditory cortex Neuropixels recording sessions — these are neural recordings, not behavioural assays per rubric (even though sounds were presented to awake mice; the primary outcome was neural activity).
Locomotion (running on wheel) was extracted from video but only used as a covariate for the neural analysis; not treated as a standalone behavioural assay.
Only the Head-Twitch Response assay (in 2 additional male mice, freely moving in home cage) is a scoreable behavioural assay with DOI administration.
Schedule set to 'repeated' because each electrophysiology mouse received DOI on 5 different days; for the HTR cohort the schedule is less clear but compound entry is study-level.
B4 scored 0: rubric explicitly excludes HTR/WDS from ethological behaviours.
E8 scored 1 (home cage implies food/water access); candidates disagreed but home-cage testing typically includes ad lib food/water.
